items.title: 5.4 Condition of Concurrency of Three Straight Lines (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book pp. 148-149: 5.4 Theorem 3 (condition of concurrency) with proof, Example 10 and a Challenge! box (missing sign corrected).

blocks.text: Assalam o alaikum bachon! Pichhle topic mein humne medians, altitudes aur right bisectors ki equations nikali thin. Ab ek naya sawal: agar teen lines hon to kya woh teeno ek hi point se guzarti hain? Jab teen ya zyada lines ek hi point se guzrein to unhein concurrent lines kehte hain, aur us common point ko point of concurrency (woh nukta jahan sab lines milti hain) kehte hain. Socho teen sarkein ek hi chowk par aa kar milti hain: woh chowk point of concurrency hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Do lines agar parallel na hon to woh hamesha sirf ek point par milti hain. Is liye teen lines ke liye asal sawal yeh hai: kya teesri line usi point se guzarti hai jahan pehli do lines milti hain? Theorem 3 is poore sawal ko ek hi number mein badal deta hai: coefficients se bana hua ek \(3 \times 3\) determinant. Agar woh zero ho to lines concurrent hain.
Theorem 3

Teen non-parallel lines (aisi lines jin mein se koi do aapas mein parallel nahi)
\[\ell_1 : a_1x + b_1y + c_1 = 0 \quad \ldots(i)\]
\[\ell_2 : a_2x + b_2y + c_2 = 0 \quad \ldots(ii)\]
\[\ell_3 : a_3x + b_3y + c_3 = 0 \quad \ldots(iii)\]
tab aur sirf tab concurrent hain (iff = if and only if) jab
\[\begin{vmatrix} a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \\ a_3 & b_3 & c_3 \end{vmatrix} = 0\]

blocks.latex: \begin{vmatrix} a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \\ a_3 & b_3 & c_3 \end{vmatrix} = 0
blocks.text_alt: The determinant with rows a1 b1 c1, a2 b2 c2 and a3 b3 c3 equals zero

blocks.text: Determinant ki har row ek line se banti hai: pehli row mein pehli line ke \(a_1, b_1, c_1\), doosri mein doosri line ke, aur teesri mein teesri line ke. Yaad rakhiye ke har line ko pehle \(ax + by + c = 0\) ki shakal mein likhna zaroori hai, warna \(c\) ka sign ghalat ho jayega.
Proof

Ab dekhte hain ke yeh shart kahan se aati hai. Agar lines concurrent hain to un ka ek common point hai; kitab use \(P(x_1, y_1)\) kehti hai. Kyunke \(\ell_1\) aur \(\ell_2\) parallel nahi \((\ell_1 \nparallel \ell_2)\), is liye in ka intersection point \((x, y)\) yeh hai:
\[x = \dfrac{b_1c_2 - b_2c_1}{a_1b_2 - a_2b_1}\]
\[y = \dfrac{a_2c_1 - a_1c_2}{a_1b_2 - a_2b_1}\]
\((\because a_1b_2 - a_2b_1 \ne 0)\)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Yeh \(x\) aur \(y\) kahan se aaye? Equations (i) aur (ii) ko Cramer's rule (ya elimination) se ek saath hal karein to yahi values aati hain. Denominator \(a_1b_2 - a_2b_1\) zero is liye nahi ke \(\ell_1\) aur \(\ell_2\) parallel nahi: un ki slopes \(-\frac{a_1}{b_1}\) aur \(-\frac{a_2}{b_2}\) alag alag hain. Agar slopes barabar hoti to \(a_1b_2 = a_2b_1\) hota aur hum divide hi na kar sakte. Kitab ne point ka naam pehle \(P(x_1, y_1)\) rakha aur phir use \((x, y)\) likha; dono se murad ek hi point hai, pareshan na hon.

Ab asal baat: yeh point teesri line (iii) par bhi hai, kyunke lines concurrent hain. Is liye is point ko (iii) mein rakhte hain:
\[a_3\left(\dfrac{b_1c_2 - b_2c_1}{a_1b_2 - a_2b_1}\right)\]
\[+ b_3\left(\dfrac{a_2c_1 - a_1c_2}{a_1b_2 - a_2b_1}\right) + c_3 = 0\]
Poori equation ko \(a_1b_2 - a_2b_1\) se multiply karein (yeh zero nahi, is liye ijazat hai), to fractions khatam ho jati hain:
\[a_3(b_1c_2 - b_2c_1)\]
\[+ b_3(a_2c_1 - a_1c_2)\]
\[+ c_3(a_1b_2 - a_2b_1) = 0\]
Is lambi equation ko chhote tareeqe se determinant ki shakal mein likh sakte hain:
\[\begin{vmatrix} a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \\ a_3 & b_3 & c_3 \end{vmatrix} = 0\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Yeh determinant wali shakal kaise bani? Determinant ko teesri row ke saath expand karein. \(a_3\), \(b_3\), \(c_3\) ke cofactors bilkul \(b_1c_2 - b_2c_1\), \(a_2c_1 - a_1c_2\) aur \(a_1b_2 - a_2b_1\) hain. Yani expansion wahi lambi equation de deti hai. Determinant sirf ek saaf suthra tareeqa hai usi baat ko likhne ka.

Yeh teen lines ke concurrent hone ki necessary aur sufficient (zaroori bhi aur kaafi bhi) shart hai. Necessary ka matlab: agar lines concurrent hain to determinant zaroor zero hoga. Sufficient ka matlab: agar determinant zero hai (aur lines non-parallel hain) to lines zaroor concurrent hongi. Dono baatein mil kar 'iff' banti hain. Proof ke poore safar ko ek jumle mein yaad rakhiye: pehli do lines ka meeting point nikalo, use teesri line mein rakho, fractions hatao, aur jo bacha woh determinant hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein jumla yun chhapa hai: 'This is necessary and sufficient condition iff of concurrency of given three lines.' Is mein 'iff' faltu hai, kyunke 'iff' ka matlab hi 'necessary and sufficient' hai. Sahi jumla: 'This is the necessary and sufficient condition for the concurrency of the given three lines.'

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Upar ka proof sirf ek taraf dikhata hai: concurrent \(\Rightarrow\) determinant \(= 0\). Ulti taraf bhi sahi hai: agar determinant zero ho aur \(\ell_1 \nparallel \ell_2\), to steps ko ulta parhein. Determinant wali equation asal mein aakhri equation ko \(a_1b_2 - a_2b_1 \ne 0\) se multiply kar ke bani thi, is liye \(\ell_1\) aur \(\ell_2\) ka meeting point (iii) ko bhi satisfy karta hai. Isi liye shart necessary bhi hai aur sufficient bhi. Lafz 'non-parallel' bahut ahem hai: teen parallel lines ka determinant bhi zero aata hai, lekin woh kabhi milti hi nahi.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Theorem 3 ko yaad karne ka aasaan tareeqa: determinant ki har row ek line ka 'shanakhti card' hai. Teen cards ek table par rakh dein; agar un se bana determinant zero ho jaye to teeno lines ek hi chowk par milti hain. Ab khud se poochiye: agar pehli do lines parallel hon to kya hoga? Jawab: phir \(a_1b_2 - a_2b_1 = 0\) ho jayega, hum proof mein divide hi nahi kar sakenge, aur meeting point hi nahi milega. Isi liye theorem mein 'non-parallel' ki shart rakhi gayi hai.

Ek aur baat samajh lein. Determinant ka zero hona asal mein yeh kehta hai ke teesri line ki equation pehli do equations se 'bani' hui hai, yani us mein koi nayi maloomat nahi. Jab teesri equation pehli do ka hi mixture ho to woh lazmi unhi ke meeting point se guzregi. Yeh baat hum agle topic 5.5 mein family of lines ki shakal mein dobara dekhenge, jahan \(\ell_1 + k\ell_2 = 0\) wali har line usi point se guzarti hai.

Ab kitab Theorem 3 ko teen di hui lines par lagati hai. Sab se pehle hum dekhte hain ke sawal kya keh raha hai: pehle check karna hai ke lines concurrent hain ya nahi, aur agar hain to point of concurrency bhi nikalna hai. Yani do kaam hain.

blocks.title: Example 10
blocks.problem:
Check whether the following lines are concurrent or not. If concurrent, then find the point of concurrency.
\[3x - 2y - 2 = 0\]
\[x + y - 4 = 0\]
\[2x - y - 2 = 0\]
steps:
Diya gaya: \(3x - 2y - 2 = 0\), \(x + y - 4 = 0\), \(2x - y - 2 = 0\).
Maloom karna: kya yeh concurrent hain, aur agar hain to point of concurrency.
Tareeqa: Theorem 3. Har line ke coefficients \(a\), \(b\), \(c\) ek row mein likh kar determinant nikalenge. Agar woh \(0\) aaye to lines concurrent hain; phir kisi bhi do lines ka meeting point hi point of concurrency hoga. Yeh tareeqa is liye munasib hai ke ek hi calculation se faisla ho jata hai.

Coefficients ka determinant likhein
\[\begin{vmatrix} 3 & -2 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & -4 \\ 2 & -1 & -2 \end{vmatrix}\]
Kyun: pehli row \(3, -2, -2\) pehli line se, doosri row \(1, 1, -4\), teesri row \(2, -1, -2\). Har constant term apne sign ke saath teesre column mein jata hai.
Dhyan dein: lines pehle se \(ax + by + c = 0\) ki shakal mein hain, is liye signs bilkul waise hi rahenge.

Pehli row ke saath expand karein
\[= 3\begin{vmatrix} 1 & -4 \\ -1 & -2 \end{vmatrix} - (-2)\begin{vmatrix} 1 & -4 \\ 2 & -2 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[- 2\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 \end{vmatrix}\]
Kyun: pehli row mein signs baari baari \(+, -, +\) hote hain. Beech wali entry \(-2\) hai, is liye us ka term \(-(-2) = +2\) guna us ka minor banta hai.
Dhyan dein: yahi minus ka minus sab se zyada ghalat hota hai.

\(2 \times 2\) minors hal karein
\[= 3(-2 - 4) + 2(-2 + 8) - 2(-1 - 2)\]
\[= 3(-6) + 2(6) - 2(-3)\]
\[= -18 + 12 + 6 = 0\]
Kyun: \(\begin{vmatrix} p & q \\ r & s \end{vmatrix} = ps - qr\). Misaal ke taur par \(\begin{vmatrix} 1 & -4 \\ -1 & -2 \end{vmatrix} = (1)(-2) - (-4)(-1) = -2 - 4 = -6\). Isi tarah baqi do minors \(6\) aur \(-3\) aate hain.

Natija
Lehaza di hui lines concurrent hain.
Kyun: determinant zero hai aur koi do lines parallel nahi (slopes \(\frac{3}{2}\), \(-1\), \(2\) teeno alag hain), is liye Theorem 3 lagta hai.

Point of concurrency nikalein
Kisi bhi do lines ka intersection point hi point of concurrency hai. \(x + y - 4 = 0\) aur \(2x - y - 2 = 0\) ko jama karein:
\[3x - 6 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 2\]
\(x = 2\) ko \(x + y - 4 = 0\) mein rakhein:
\[2 + y - 4 = 0 \Rightarrow y = 2\]
Lehaza \((2, 2)\) point of concurrency hai.
Kyun: ek equation mein \(+y\) aur doosri mein \(-y\) hai, jama karne se \(y\) foran cancel ho jata hai; yeh sab se tez elimination hai.

Tasdeeq:
\((2, 2)\) ko teeno lines mein rakh kar dekhein:
\[3(2) - 2(2) - 2 = 0\]
\[2 + 2 - 4 = 0\]
\[2(2) - 2 - 2 = 0\]
Teeno poori ho gayin, yani point har line par hai.
blocks.answer: The determinant is \(0\), so the lines are concurrent; the point of concurrency is \((2, 2)\).

blocks.text: Is misaal se kya seekha? Pehle determinant ne bataya ke lines concurrent hain ya nahi; yeh 'haan ya na' wala faisla tha. Phir point nikalne ke liye humne sirf do lines hal kin, kyunke teesri line to khud ba khud usi point se guzregi. Aakhir mein tasdeeq ne dono kaamon ko pakka kar diya. Exam mein yahi teen qadam likhenge to poore number milenge: determinant, natija, aur point (agar poocha gaya ho).

blocks.title: Challenge!
blocks.text: Agar lines \(2x - 3y + 5 = 0\), \(3x + 4y - 1 = 0\) aur \(kx - 7y + 6 = 0\) concurrent hon to \(k\) ki value maloom karein.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Challenge ki pehli line kitab mein \(2x \quad 3y + 5 = 0\) chhapi hai: \(2x\) aur \(3y\) ke darmiyan sign ghayab hai. Sahi line \(2x - 3y + 5 = 0\) hai. Minus ke saath \(2x - 3y + 5 = 0\) aur \(3x + 4y - 1 = 0\) point \((-1, 1)\) par milti hain aur sawal saaf hal hota hai. (Plus ke saath lines \((23, -17)\) par milti aur \(k = -\frac{125}{23}\) aata, jo zahir hai kitab ka maqsad nahi.)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Khud sochiye: pehle Challenge khud hal karne ki koshish karein, phir yahan dekhein. Theorem 3 se:
\[\begin{vmatrix} 2 & -3 & 5 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 \\ k & -7 & 6 \end{vmatrix} = 0\]
\[2(24 - 7) + 3(18 + k) + 5(-21 - 4k) = 0\]
\[34 + 54 + 3k - 105 - 20k = 0\]
\[-17 - 17k = 0 \Rightarrow k = -1\]
Tasdeeq: pehli do lines \((-1, 1)\) par milti hain, aur \((-1)(-1) - 7(1) + 6 = 0\). Bilkul theek.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Kya lines \(x + y - 2 = 0\), \(x - y = 0\) aur \(2x + y - 3 = 0\) concurrent hain?
\[\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & -3 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(3 - 0) - 1(-3 - 0) - 2(1 + 2)\]
\[= 3 + 3 - 6 = 0\]
Determinant zero hai, to lines concurrent hain. Pehli do lines jama karne se \(2x = 2\), yani \(x = 1\), \(y = 1\). Teesri mein: \(2 + 1 - 3 = 0\). Point of concurrency \((1, 1)\) hai.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text:
Concurrency check karne ke do tareeqe hain:
1. Determinant wala tareeqa (Theorem 3): ek hi calculation; jab sawal 'check' karne ya '\(k\) nikalne' ka ho to kitab yahi tareeqa chahti hai.
2. Point wala tareeqa: do lines hal karein, phir woh point teesri line mein rakhein.
Jab point of concurrency bhi poocha ho to point wala kaam to karna hi parega; use determinant ki tasdeeq ke taur par bhi istemal karein.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Concurrent lines ek hi common point se guzarti hain, jise point of concurrency kehte hain.
2. Theorem 3: teen non-parallel lines \(a_ix + b_iy + c_i = 0\) tab aur sirf tab concurrent hain jab coefficients ka determinant zero ho.
3. Determinant wali equation asal mein pehli do lines ka meeting point teesri line mein rakhne se banti hai, \(a_1b_2 - a_2b_1\) se multiply kar ke.
4. Point of concurrency kisi bhi do lines ko hal kar ke milta hai.
5. Concurrency ke liye na-maloom \(k\) nikalna ho to determinant ko zero ke barabar rakh kar \(k\) hal karein.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Lines ko \(ax + by = c\) ki shakal mein likh kar \(c\) seedha determinant mein daal dena: theorem \(ax + by + c = 0\) wali shakal par hai, constant ko doosri taraf le jayen to us ka sign badal jata hai.
2. Row ke saath expand karte waqt beech wale term ka minus sign bhool jana.
3. Teen parallel lines ko sirf is liye concurrent keh dena ke determinant zero aaya: theorem ke liye lines non-parallel honi chahiye.
4. Sirf 'determinant \(= 0\)' likh kar ruk jana jab sawal point of concurrency bhi maang raha ho.
